}.spent)57        assertEquals(2000L, amounts.first { it.category.id == "food" }.remaining)58    }59    @Test fun monthEndDatesRecoverAndStartEndPauseAreRespected() {60        val value = rule("rent", archive.readEncrypted(ByteArrayInputStream(output.toByteArray()), "Version five test password".toCharArray()).use { prepared ->475            assertEquals(original, prepared.backup)476            assertEquals(original, archive.materialize(prepared))477        }478    }479480}

{}138        assertArrayEquals(before, legacyFile.readBytes())139        assertFalse(encryptedFile.exists())140    }141    @Test fun lastExpensePaymentSurvivesEncryptedStoreRestartWithOtherPreferencesIntact() = runBlocking {142        var active = scope()143        var store = SettingsStore(context, vault, active)144        assertEquals("Cash", store.settings.first().lastExpensePayment)145        for (payment in expensePaymentOptions) {146            val settings = AppSettings(theme = "Dark", receiptSaveMode = "Smart", 1package my.fuelledger.ui23import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Color4import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.luminance5import org.junit.Assert.assertTrue6import org.junit.Test78class ClarityContrastTest {9    private fun readable(label: String, foreground: Color, background: Color) {10        val first = foreground.luminance(); val second = background.luminance()11        val contrast = (maxOf(first, second) + .05f) / (minOf(first, second) + .05f)12        assertTrue("$label must meet normal-text contrast: $contrast", contrast >= 4.5f)13    }14    @Test fun primaryAndSecondaryTextRemainReadableInBothThemesAndTheNavyDashboard() {15        for ((name, colors) in listOf("Light" to LedgerLightColors, "Dark" to LedgerDarkColors)) {16            readable("$name background", colors.onBackground, colors.background)17            readable("$name card", colors.onSurface, colors.surfaceContainer)18            readable("$name muted label", colors.onSurfaceVariant, colors.surfaceContainer)19            readable("$name primary button", colors.onPrimary, colors.primary)20            readable("$name selected control", colors.onPrimaryContainer, colors.primaryContainer)21        }22        readable("Dashboard primary", DashboardColors.primary, DashboardColors.surface)23        readable("Dashboard secondary", DashboardColors.secondary, DashboardColors.surface)24    }25}

1package my.fuelledger.build;23import com.android.build.api.instrumentation.AsmClassVisitorFactory;4import com.android.build.api.instrumentation.ClassContext;5import com.android.build.api.instrumentation.ClassData;6import com.android.build.api.instrumentation.InstrumentationParameters;7import java.util.Map;8import java.util.Collection;9import java.util.HashSet;10import java.util.Set;11import java.io.File;12import java.io.IOException;13import java.util.jar.JarInputStream;14import java.util.zip.ZipFile;15import org.objectweb.asm.ClassReader;16import org.objectweb.asm.ClassWriter;17import org.objectweb.asm.ClassVisitor;18import org.objectweb.asm.MethodVisitor;19import org.objectweb.asm.Opcodes;20import org.objectweb.asm.Type;2122/**23 * Removes ML Kit's Firelog and Play Services telemetry sinks in both APK variants.24 * OCR/model code is untouched. No reflection, runtime SDK patch, or network fallback.25 * Targets are reviewed against the pinned SDKs; dependency changes require a new audit.26 */27public abstract class OfflineMlKitTelemetry implements AsmClassVisitorFactory<InstrumentationParameters.None> {28    public static final Map<String, String> TARGETS = Map.of(29        "com.google.android.gms.internal.mlkit_common.zzsp", "zzsb;Lcom/google/android/gms/internal/mlkit_common/zzry;",30        "com.google.android.gms.internal.mlkit_vision_common.zzmp", "zzme;Lcom/google/android/gms/internal/mlkit_vision_common/zzmb;",31        "com.google.android.gms.internal.mlkit_vision_text_common.zzuk", "zztu;Lcom/google/android/gms/internal/mlkit_vision_text_common/zztr;",32        "com.google.android.gms.internal.mlkit_vision_text_common.zzue", "GMS_TELEMETRY"33    );3435    @Override public boolean isInstrumentable(ClassData data) { return TARGETS.containsKey(data.getClassName()); }3637    @Override public ClassVisitor createClassVisitor(ClassContext context, ClassVisitor next) {38        return visitor(context.getCurrentClassData().getClassName(), next);39    }4041    /** Fail the build when pinned SDKs stop supplying any reviewed telemetry sink. */42    public static void verifyAars(Collection<File> archives) throws IOException {43        Set<String> found = new HashSet<>();44        for (File archive : archives) {45            if (!archive.getName().endsWith(".aar")) continue;46            try (ZipFile zip = new ZipFile(archive)) {47                var entry = zip.getEntry("classes.jar");48                if (entry == null) continue;49                try (JarInputStream jar = new JarInputStream(zip.getInputStream(entry))) {50                    java.util.jar.JarEntry cls;51                    while ((cls = jar.getNextJarEntry()) != null) {52                        String name = cls.getName().replace('/', '.').replaceFirst("\\.class$", "");53                        if (!TARGETS.containsKey(name)) continue;54                        if (!found.add(name)) throw new IllegalStateException("Duplicate reviewed ML Kit sink: " + name);55                        new ClassReader(jar).accept(visitor(name, new ClassWriter(0)), 0);56                    }57                }58            }59        }60        if (!found.equals(TARGETS.keySet()))61            throw new IllegalStateException("ML Kit dependencies changed; review offline telemetry policy: " + found);62    }6364    public static ClassVisitor visitor(String name, ClassVisitor next) {65        if (!TARGETS.containsKey(name)) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Unreviewed ML Kit telemetry class");66        String prefix = name.substring(0, name.lastIndexOf('.') + 1).replace('.', '/');67        boolean gms = TARGETS.get(name).equals("GMS_TELEMETRY");68        String[] types = TARGETS.get(name).split(";L");69        String constructor = gms ? "(Landroid/content/Context;Ljava/lang/String;)V"70            : "(Landroid/content/Context;L" + prefix + types[0] + ";)V";71        String dispatch = gms ? "(IIJJ)V" : "(L" + types[1] + ")V";72        return new ClassVisitor(Opcodes.ASM9, next) {73            private int constructors;74            private int sends;75            @Override public MethodVisitor visitMethod(int access, String method, String descriptor,76                    String signature, String[] exceptions) {77                MethodVisitor output = super.visitMethod(access, method, descriptor, signature, exceptions);78                boolean init = method.equals("<init>");79                boolean send = (gms ? method.equals("zzb") || method.equals("zzc") : method.equals("zza"))80                    && (access & Opcodes.ACC_STATIC) == 0;81                if (!init && !send) return output;82                String expectedDispatch = gms && method.equals("zzb") ? "(JLjava/lang/Exception;)V" : dispatch;83                if ((init && !descriptor.equals(constructor)) || (send && !descriptor.equals(expectedDispatch)))84                    throw new IllegalStateException("ML Kit telemetry signature changed; review offline build policy: " + name);85                if (init) constructors++; else sends++;86                // Drop the original implementation completely, including all transport startup.87                return new MethodVisitor(Opcodes.ASM9) {88                    @Override public void visitEnd() {89                        output.visitCode();90                        if (init) {91                            output.visitVarInsn(Opcodes.ALOAD, 0);92                            output.visitMethodInsn(Opcodes.INVOKESPECIAL, "java/lang/Object", "<init>", "()V", false);93                        }94                        output.visitInsn(Opcodes.RETURN);95                        output.visitMaxs(init ? 1 : 0, Type.getArgumentsAndReturnSizes(descriptor) >> 2);96                        output.visitEnd();97                    }98                };99            }100            @Override public void visitEnd() {101                if (constructors != 1 || sends != (gms ? 2 : 1))102                    throw new IllegalStateException("ML Kit telemetry shape changed; review offline build policy: " + name);103                super.visitEnd();104            }105        };106    }107}

docs/audit-2026-10-18/RELEASE_NOTES.md

Pinned GitHub source

1### New features23- None. This release audits and maintains the existing offline application.45### Bug fixes67- Reject Undo when later refunds would exceed the restored purchase amount; keep the current record and Undo entry intact.8- Reject linking a refund as payment of a fixed commitment, and validate the resulting expense before storing it.9- Add native production-Activity readiness and recreation acceptance coverage alongside the encrypted-storage tests.1011### UI improvements1213- Preserve existing screen layout, typography, pager gestures, theme behavior and independent Settings switch updates.14- Remove unused imports, two unused generated name/version strings and the empty custom ProGuard file.15- Remove empty Room/WorkManager KTX compatibility artifacts; retain their active runtime libraries and versions.16- Share fuel-point validation, reuse transaction snapshots and replace repeated refund scans with ID lookups without changing formulas or data formats.

1# Full Android Project Audit, Cleanup and Code Optimization23Act as a senior Android software architect, Kotlin developer, code reviewer and QA engineer.45Perform a COMPLETE review of my existing Android Fuel & Expense Tracker project.67The project has undergone many development iterations, UI redesigns, bug fixes and feature additions. I want the codebase to be clean, organized, maintainable and free of unnecessary files.89**Important: Review the entire repository, not just the most recently modified files.**1011## 1. Complete Project Inspection1213Inspect all relevant project files, including:1415- Kotlin source files.16- Jetpack Compose UI components.17- ViewModels.18- Repositories.19- Room database entities, DAOs and migrations.20- Navigation components.21- Calculation utilities.22- Gradle configuration.23- AndroidManifest.xml.24- Resources, icons and images.25- Assets and fonts.26- Automated tests.27- Documentation.28- Build scripts.29- Release configurations.3031Identify unused, duplicated, obsolete or unrelated content.3233## 2. Remove Unnecessary Files3435Identify and remove genuinely unnecessary content, including:3637- Unused Kotlin files and classes.38- Abandoned UI components.39- Obsolete screens from earlier designs.40- Duplicate functions and utilities.41- Unused drawable resources.42- Unreferenced icons and images.43- Temporary development files.44- Accidental backup copies.45- Obsolete generated files.46- Unused dependencies.47- Outdated sample data embedded in production code.48- Unnecessary debugging code.49- Unrelated files not required by the project.5051Do not remove files merely because they are not directly referenced by another Kotlin file. Check manifest entries, resource references, reflection, build configuration, tests and runtime usage.5253## 3. Protect Important Project Files5455DO NOT delete:5657- Active source code.58- Database migration history.59- Existing user data.60- Signing keys or configurations required for updates.61- Necessary Gradle configuration.62- Required Android resources.63- Current tests.64- Encrypted backup functionality.65- Necessary licenses and documentation.66- Historical APK releases intentionally retained.67- Files required by dynamically loaded components.6869Do not expose signing keys, passwords or sensitive information in logs or reports.7071Before deleting anything:721. Create a Git checkpoint if available.732. Identify files that are safe to remove.743. Distinguish definite junk from uncertain files.754. Delete only files verified to be unnecessary.765. Leave uncertain files unchanged and report them.7778## 4. Review Code Quality7980Inspect the entire codebase for:8182- Duplicate logic.83- Unused imports.84- Unused variables.85- Unreachable code.86- Overly complex functions.87- Repeated Compose components.88- Inconsistent naming.89- Unnecessary state management.90- Potential memory leaks.91- Unnecessary recompositions.92- Inefficient database queries.93- Excessive object allocations.94- Deprecated APIs.95- Redundant dependencies.9697Refactor where appropriate.9899Avoid unnecessary architectural rewrites.100101Keep the existing application behaviour unchanged unless fixing a verified defect.102103## 5. Check Existing Features104105Ensure the cleanup preserves all current features:106107- Home dashboard.108- Expenses and income.109- Spending Calendar.110- Fuel Tracker.111- Journey Planner.112- Analysis.113- Monthly Money Planner.114- Fixed recurring expenses.115- Receipt Scanner.116- Home-screen widgets.117- Light, Dark and System themes.118- Horizontal swipe navigation.119- App lock and privacy features.120- Encrypted local backup.121- Financial report export.122123Inspect existing functionality rather than assuming every listed feature is already implemented.124125## 6. Optimize Jetpack Compose126127Review:128- Shared UI components.129- Theme consistency.130- Animation performance.131- Recomposition behaviour.132- Modifier chains.133- State management.134- Navigation lifecycle.135- Gesture handling.136- HorizontalPager integration.137138Remove duplicated visual components where reusable shared components are appropriate.139140Ensure all five main screens maintain consistent sizing and spacing.141142Do not reintroduce the previous Journey screen scaling problem or the Settings switch blinking issue.143144## 7. Database and Calculation Safety145146Review financial and fuel calculations carefully.147148Ensure:149- Expenses are not double-counted.150- Fuel expenses remain correctly linked.151- Recurring transactions are not duplicated.152- Budget calculations remain accurate.153- Historical fuel estimates use the intended calculation method.154- Database migrations remain compatible.155- Existing records are never silently removed.156157Do not delete database entities or fields simply because they are no longer visible in the UI.158159Preserve historical data compatibility.160161## 8. Offline Security Audit162163Confirm that the application remains completely offline.164165Verify:166- No INTERNET permission in the merged manifest.167- No unwanted network SDKs.168- No Firebase or cloud synchronization.169- No unnecessary analytics or telemetry.170- No sensitive data exposed in logs.171- No accidental cloud backups.172- Receipt recognition uses bundled on-device processing.173174Remove unused dependencies that could introduce unnecessary security or privacy risks.175176## 9. Gradle and Build Cleanup177178Review:179- Unused Gradle plugins.180- Unnecessary dependencies.181- Duplicated dependency declarations.182- Outdated configuration.183- Unused build scripts.184- Incorrect version references.185186Ensure the project builds reproducibly.187188Update .gitignore where necessary so disposable build outputs and local machine-specific files are not committed.189190Do not delete intentionally retained APK releases or signing materials.191192## 10. Testing After Cleanup193194Run available:195- Kotlin compilation.196- Android Gradle build.197- Unit tests.198- Android Lint.199- Relevant UI tests.200201Verify:202- Main navigation works.203- Financial calculations remain accurate.204- Fuel calculations remain functional.205- Room migrations remain safe.206- The receipt scanner remains functional.207- Appearance settings persist.208- Screenshots remain enabled.209- The application still works offline.210211Fix errors introduced by cleanup.212213## 11. Project Organization214215Organize the codebase using the existing architecture.216217Prefer clear feature boundaries and shared components.218219For example:220- home221- expenses222- fuel223- journey224- analysis225- settings226- data227- domain228- core229- ui/theme230231Do not move everything into new packages merely for appearance.232233Refactor only when it materially improves maintainability.234235## 12. Final Audit Report236237After cleanup, provide:2382391. Files reviewed.2402. Files deleted and reasons.2413. Duplicate code removed.2424. Unused dependencies removed.2435. Code optimizations completed.2446. Project structure improvements.2457. Potential issues discovered.2468. Issues fixed.2479. Uncertain files intentionally retained.24810. Build and test results.24911. Confirmation that existing app data and functionality were preserved.250251Create a CLEANUP_REPORT.md documenting these findings.252253## 13. Version Management254255If the cleanup results in a verified release-worthy change:256- Update the app version appropriately.257- Increment versionCode.258- Update CHANGELOG.md.259- Preserve applicationId and signing compatibility.260- Build an updated APK if the environment supports it.261262Do not change the version solely because an unsuccessful build was attempted.263264## Final Objective265266Deliver a clean, organized, efficient and maintainable Android project without unnecessary files or obsolete code.267268Prioritize:2691. Data preservation.2702. Functional correctness.2713. Safe cleanup.2724. Code maintainability.2735. Performance.2746. Build stability.275276Do not add unrelated new features.277278**Begin by auditing the complete repository, then safely perform the cleanup and verify the results.**

1# PROJECT: CLARITY — Complete Android UI/UX Refinement23## Role45Act as an expert Android UI/UX designer, senior Jetpack Compose developer and mobile design-system architect.67I want to improve the visual design, interaction quality and usability of my EXISTING Fuel & Expense Tracker application.89The objective is a premium, minimalist Android application similar in quality to a professionally designed financial management product.1011**Do not rebuild the project. Do not add unrelated features. Focus on design quality and implementation accuracy.**1213Use the provided design reference screenshot, if attached, as the visual source of truth for the Home screen.1415Preserve:16- All existing financial data.17- Current database and migrations.18- Working financial calculations.19- Existing feature functionality.20- Fully offline operation.21- App signing compatibility.22- Light, Dark and System themes.2324---2526# 1. DESIGN PHILOSOPHY2728Design concept: CLARITY.2930Core principles:31321. Minimalist, not empty.332. Premium, not decorative.343. Functional, not overloaded.354. Consistent across all screens.365. Fast for repetitive daily usage.376. One clear primary action per context.387. Display numbers more prominently than descriptions.398. No duplicated controls or settings.409. No unnecessary borders or visual effects.4110. Use actual application data, not hardcoded demonstration values.4243Avoid generic Android tutorial styling.4445Avoid overly large cards, unnecessary gradients, excessive shadows, large blank spaces and repetitive explanatory text.4647The interface should look polished and intentional.4849---5051# 2. 1# Journey layout investigation — 16 October 202623Baseline: commit `313d66e`. This is a UI-only correction of the existing app. Home, Fuel and Expenses are the reference; their rendered screenshots remain byte-for-byte unchanged in the three configurations captured before and after this fix.45## Actual causes671. `JourneyScreen` used `PaddingValues(20.dp)`, while the reference screens used 20dp horizontal, 8dp top and 28dp bottom padding. Journey's heading therefore started **12dp too low**.82. `LocationSuggestions` always emitted a `Row`, even with no matching locations. `LedgerCard` uses a Column with 14dp spacing; each empty row still added another spaced slot. The measured Origin-to-Destination gap was **28dp instead of 14dp**. Two empty rows added 28dp to the form.93. The long heading **Journey Planner** wrapped at 320dp into two lines (64px measured text bounds versus 30px for the reference headings). The redundant **One-way / outbound distance (km)** label also wrapped, increasing that input's height. Input `singleLine` governs entered text, not the independently laid-out label.104. The form-card title and estimated-total label both used `titleLarge` (22sp/30sp line height), unlike existing form-card headings (`titleMedium`, 16sp/24sp) and hero labels (`labelLarge`, 14sp/20sp). Their semantic roles now use those existing styles. The prominent cost amount remains 36sp/44sp, matching the dashboard hero amount.1112These were accumulated layout height and text-wrapping differences, not a global zoom, altered display density or different theme.1314## Implementation comparison1516| Property | Home / Fuel / Expenses | Journey before → after |17| --- | --- | --- |18| Root / width | LazyColumn under the app's shared Box/Crossfade; constrained by the same viewport | Same; unchanged |19| Horizontal margins | 20dp each side | Already 20dp; unchanged |20| Top / bottom content padding | 8dp / 28dp | 20dp / 20dp → same shared 8dp / 28dp |21| Heading | Shared ScreenHeading, 26sp/34sp; 46dp icon, 24dp glyph, 48dp Settings touch target | Same component and sizes; shorter visible title “Journey” prevents unnecessary wrapping |22| Card width / shape | Available width minus 40dp; LedgerCard 22dp radius | Already identical; unchanged |23| Card padding / child spacing | 20dp / 14dp in LedgerCard | Unchanged; empty suggestion rows no longer add extra gaps |24| Between list items | Home/Fuel 16dp; Expenses 14dp | 16dp, matching Home/Fuel; unchanged |25| Input controls | Shared TextField/NumericField wrapping Material OutlinedTextField; bodyLarge 16sp/24sp, 56dp minimum surface | Same controls; shorter labels preserve units/context and avoid wrapping at normal font sizes |26| Buttons | Shared Material adapters; LedgerAction and Journey toggle use 56dp minimum, standard Material controls retain accessible minimum touch targets | Existing shared buttons and 56dp toggle unchanged |27| Scrolling | One vertical LazyColumn; nested horizontal rows where needed | Same; explicit list state retained for Edit/load scrolling; suggestions remain horizontal |28| Scaffold / bars / navigation | One LedgerApp Scaffold owns status/system insets and bottom navigation | Same instance and destination order; no nested Scaffold or inset modifiers added |29| Theme / density / scale | LedgerTheme / LedgerTypography; inherited Android density/font scale | Identical; no local density override or whole-screen scaling |30| Press feedback | Shared draw-only 0.97× feedback while pressed | Unchanged; cannot explain the resting layout difference |3132Shortened field labels are **Outbound distance (km)**, **Fallback (L/100 km)**, **Override (L/100 km)** and **Parking (RM)**. Input validation, state, saved values and callbacks are unchanged. Suggestions retain the exact filtering, limit and click behavior; only the empty layout container is omitted.3334## Measured result3536At 393×851dp, mdpi, font scale 1.0:3738| Measurement | Before Journey | After Journey | Reference |39| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |40| Heading text left / top | 80 / 27px | 80 / 15px | 80 / 15px |41| Heading text height | 30px | 30px | 30px |42| Field left / width | 40 / 313px | 40 / 313px | Expenses search: 40 / 313px |43| Origin field height | 65px | 65px | Expenses search: 65px |44| Origin → Destination gap | 28px | 14px | LedgerCard spacing: 14dp |45| Bottom navigation viewport | y=771–851px | y=771–851px | y=771–851px |4647At 320×640dp, Journey now has one heading line and a 65px outbound field, matching its Origin field and the Expenses search field. Its heading starts at y=15px, matching Home/Expenses (Fuel is y=14px due to its naturally wrapping subtitle). No text size, device density or touch target is artificially scaled down.4849The 65px text-field semantic height includes the Material label allowance above the 56dp outlined surface; it is not a custom enlarged control.5051## Matched screenshots5253All images come from the actual MainActivity and its real navigation, rendered with Robolectric native graphics on API35. Each row uses exactly the same viewport, density, font scale and theme for all four screens. Screenshots are captured after navigation/theme transitions settle. Screenshots are test artifacts, not receipts or real financial records.6364## Verification and limits6566Signed debug and optimized unsigned release APKs build successfully. Release vital lint and debug/release 16KiB ZIP alignment checks pass. Debug lint has 0 errors, the same 10 advisory warnings and 1 hint as the baseline: six preserved unused app-name/version entries, one SQLite update suggestion, one state-backed offset suggestion, two KTX suggestions and one primitive-state hint. Native API26 in-place installation succeeds without clearing data; launch reports `Status: ok`, and MainActivity is confirmed as the resumed foreground activity. This native check covers startup, not a rerun of the historical financial/OCR instrumentation suite.6768The large-font run revealed an existing shared-navigation behavior: long Expenses/Analytics labels wrap at 160% font scale on every screen. This is not Journey-specific; the shared navigation is intentionally unchanged. Large accessibility text can naturally increase component heights and scrolling. Reference screen item spacing remains 14dp for Expenses versus 16dp for Home/Fuel/Journey. These existing differences are documented rather than altering the reference screens.6970Host screenshots do not validate every OEM/font/density combination, physical keyboard, TalkBack or on-device system-bar rendering. There is no known Journey-specific clipping/overlap in the inspected configurations; content below the viewport remains available by scrolling.7172## Modified implementation files7374- `ui/JourneyScreen.kt`: shared padding, no empty suggestion rows, concise heading/labels and appropriate existing card text roles.75- `ui/Components.kt`: moved the exact existing screen-padding value into an internal shared token.76- `ui/Screens.kt`: reference screens use the relocated token with identical values and rendering; no layout redesign.77- `ui/AppSmokeTest.kt`: selectors updated for the concise labels; existing calculation/save/load assertions retained.78- `ui/JourneyLayoutTest.kt`: matched real-app captures and geometry regression tests, including small phones and Android 160% font scaling.79- `README.md`, `PROGRESS.md`, `VALIDATION.md`, this report and screenshot evidence, plus the new APK and checksum.8081No changes to JourneyViewModel, journey formulas/data classes, toll computation, Room entities/migrations, saved journeys, permissions, security, dependencies, app name/version or navigation order.

original certificate", sourceCheckpoint=subprocess.check_output(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], cwd=root, text=True).strip() if (root / ".git").exists() else "test-fixture")129    history.append(record)130    entry = f"\n## {version} — {release_date}\n\n{notes.strip()}\n"131    atomic_text(history_path, json.dumps(history, indent=2) + "\n")132    atomic_text(root / "RELEASES.md", render_releases(history))133    atomic_text(root / "CHANGELOG.md", "# Changelog\n" + entry + old_changelog[len("# Changelog\n"):])134    sums = "\n".join(f"{hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()}  {p.name}" for p in sorted((root / "downloads").glob("*.apk"))) + "\n"135    atomic_text(root / "downloads/SHA256SUMS", sums)136    atomic_text(root / "version.properties", f"# Last successfully verified distributable APK.
